title: Mastering Zonular Dehiscence: Diagnosis, Mechanics, and Management
summary: Zonular dehiscence involves the focal or diffuse loss of the suspensory ligaments of the lens, leading to subluxation or dislocation. This critical complication demands precise surgical planning to avoid intraoperative catastrophes.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Zonular dehiscence is the rupture or lysis of the ciliary zonules (Zinn's zonules), which connect the lens capsule to the ciliary body. A loss of <90 degrees is often focal; >180 degrees typically results in significant lens subluxation or phacodonesis. Failure to recognize preoperative dehiscence during phacoemulsification significantly increases the risk of vitreous loss and capsular bag drop.

sections.title: Clinical Examination Findings
content: Phacodonesis: Lens wobble on rapid eye movement
Iridodonesis: Tremulous iris indicating loss of lens support
Vitreous in Anterior Chamber: Direct sign of zonular gap
Asymmetric Anterior Chamber Depth: Deepening in the area of dehiscence
Lens Subluxation: Visible lens edge or equatorial notch

sections.title: Red Flags: Impending Complications
content: Preoperative identification of vitreous prolapse through the zonular defect.
Deep chamber and tremulous iris suggesting >6 clock hours of zonular loss.
Intraoperative 'shallow' chamber during phaco—sign of posterior pressure/vitreous force.
Sudden radial capsular tear progression during rhexis.
Significant lens tilt post-implant.

sections.title: Surgical Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Mydriasis and stabilization with heavy OVDs (e.g., Healon5).
Step 2: Utilization of Capsular Tension Rings (CTR) for <3-4 clock hours.
Step 3: If >4 clock hours, utilize Cionni modified CTR or Ahmed Segment.
Step 4: Consider scleral fixation of the CTR/segment using Gore-Tex or Prolene.
Step 5: Minimal flow/vacuum parameters during phaco to minimize zonular stress.
Step 6: Pars Plana Vitrectomy if vitreous is present or suspected.

content.explanation: Z: Zero/Mild (Standard IOL); O: Observed (CTR); N: Needs fixation (Cionni/Segment); S: Severe/Aphakia (AC IOL/Scleral Fixated IOL/Yamane).

sections.title: Recent Advances: The Yamane Technique
content: Double-needle intrascleral haptic fixation (Yamane technique).
Eliminates need for large incisions or scleral flaps.
Reduces incidence of endophthalmitis and suture-related erosions.
Current gold standard for severe zonulopathy or aphakia.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: Always stain the capsule with Trypan Blue; zonular dehiscence makes the capsule difficult to visualize.
Do not over-fill with OVD in suspected PXE—can push the lens further posteriorly.
If the rhexis pulls toward the dehiscence, stop immediately—use capsule hooks to stabilize.
In Marfan patients, consider early surgery due to high risk of glaucoma secondary to pupillary block.
